Reuters —
France reported the first human case of the Shamonda virus usually found in livestock on Thursday in a hospital patient who died, though authorities said there was no risk to the general population.
It is suspected that the victim was bitten by a midge carrying the virus in eastern France where it had circulated among animals this spring and summer, the government said in a statement.
The man had been hospitalized in Lyon with an unrelated serious disease, a French health ministry official told reporters. ...

Cape Town, South AfricaAP —
A foreign citizen was beaten to death by a group of around 50 people during a protest march in South Africa’s east coast city of Durban, police said Thursday, as anti-immigrant tensions continue to flare in Africa’s most advanced economy.
Police said the group approached the man, who was standing at the side of a road during a march through the streets of Durban’s city center, and assaulted him.

item.title: Lions are being poisoned in revenge attacks. Maasai warriors are trying to end the killings
item.description: Lions in Kenya and Tanzania are being poisoned in retaliation for livestock attacks. Maasai conservationists are working to curb human-lion conflict.

item.title: A small but powerful African nation is bringing F1 back to the continent. Not everyone is celebrating
item.description: Formula One is to return to Africa for the first time in more than three decades, with Rwanda granted a 10-year contract to host a Grand Prix from the early 2030s – a deal described by F1 chief Stefano Domenicali as a “landmark” moment.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro inherited his father’s right-wing movement. Can he win Brazil’s presidency?
item.description: Flávio faces a task that even his father could not accomplish: defeating Brazil’s leftist President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who, at nearly 80, is seeking a fourth and likely final term.

item.title: Two men rearrested on suspicion of assisting Iran’s intelligence service in RAF Fairford incident
item.description: British counterterrorism police said Tuesday they have rearrested two men in their investigation into last month’s incident at RAF Fairford in England, where US B-1 bombers were based.

item.title: Macron slams ‘stupid comments’ from world leaders after Trump blames France unrest on migrants
item.description: France’s President Emmanuel Macron has slammed what he called “stupid comments” from some world leaders over the recent protests sweeping the country, after his US counterpart Donald Trump claimed migrants were fueling the unrest.
